Class BotProfile

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.curriculum.BotProfile
public final class BotProfile extends Object
How the sparring bot is placed and how it behaves in one stage. Plain public fields so the whole thing round-trips through the JSON config.

    • wtap

    • followUpTicks

      public int followUpTicks
      Above zero: the bot keeps a combo going. For this many ticks after landing a hit it swings again the moment the agent is in its reach and its weapon is back, with no reaction time in between, the way a player follows up a hit on a rhythm rather than on sight. An agent that walks back into it is hit again; one that backs away until this has run out meets the slow bot again.

    • followUpReach

      public float followUpReach
      Extra reach, in blocks, of those follow-up swings. A player with a combo going lands hits the other cannot answer: the one being hit is in the air or on its way out, and on a server it is hit where it was a moment ago. With this the bot's follow-up cannot be traded with either; what is left is getting out of it.

    • followUpWhiff

      public float followUpWhiff
      Above zero: a follow-up swing is thrown on rhythm, whether or not it will land. As soon as the weapon is back and the agent is no farther than this many blocks beyond its reach, it swings. At an agent that has backed out, that swing misses: the combo is over, the weapon is recharging and the bot is open to a charged hit. That opening is what backing out of a combo is for; without it the bot only ever swings when it will land, and nothing the agent does gets it one.

    • swingSlip

      public float swingSlip
      The chance that a swing of its own comes late: it has the agent in reach and under its crosshair, its weapon is back, and it takes one to swingSlipTicks ticks more to swing. A person does that every few swings, also in the middle of a combo, and for those ticks stands within the agent's reach with nothing on the way. A swing back made then lands first and ends the combo. Without it the scripted opponent's follow-up came on the first tick it could, every time, and a swing back was never worth making. Not for a swing made on the way down from a jump: that one has five ticks to be made in.

    • dodgeChance

      public float dodgeChance
      The chance, each time the agent hits it, that it backs straight off for a moment instead of walking back in: what a person does who wants out of a combo.

    • dodgeTicks

      public int dodgeTicks

    • critChance

      public float critChance
      Share of its swings, when the agent is close, that the bot makes as a jumped critical hit instead: it stops sprinting, jumps and swings on the way down.

    • critPress

      public float critPress
      Share of its critical hits after which it keeps coming, running straight at the agent for half a second instead of holding its range or backing off: what a player does who wants to stay on top of the one they have just hit. A critical hit throws the agent back only a little, so with this the bot is still in the agent's reach as the agent comes down, and there is a punish crit to be made. Without it there never was one: the bot was gone before the agent had landed.

    • fleeChance

      public float fleeChance
      The chance, each time it lands a hit or takes one, that it runs: for a second or two it makes for somewhere away from the agent. What a player does who keeps running out of a fight. Most times it backs off with its eyes on the agent and its sword ready: a run closes on that only slowly, a running jump twice as fast, and it hits a fighter that comes in on it carelessly. The rest (fleeTurned) it turns its back and sprints: it cannot swing then, and a fighter that only sprints after it never gets any nearer, since both run as fast. Either way the hit made coming down from a running jump, with the sprint let go, is a critical hit, which does not send the runner on its way as a sprint hit would.

    • fleeTurned

      public float fleeTurned

    • orbit

      public boolean orbit
      It fights by going round the agent: it keeps to about two blocks, walks sideways round it, changing direction now and then, and makes its hits as jumped critical hits from there. A critical hit throws the agent up and hardly back, so it comes down with this opponent still in reach, but no longer where its crosshair was.

    • fleeUntilHit

      public boolean fleeUntilHit
      A run does not end by itself: it keeps away from the agent until the agent has hit it, turning its back whenever the agent comes near and looking back at it from a distance. What a player does who will not be caught. Only a fighter that covers ground faster than a run gets to it.

    • holdGround

      public boolean holdGround
      It does not walk: it stands where it was put (in a corner, with the wall behind it), turns to face the agent and hits it whenever it comes into reach, jumping for its critical hits on the spot. A hit does not send it anywhere, so what decides the fight is what each hit does.

    • jumpIn

      public boolean jumpIn
      It combos with sprint hits from the edge of its reach, and an agent that backs off out of that reach it comes after with a running jump, taken from as far off as the way down will bring the agent into reach (four blocks from one that is walking backwards): it sprints up to the top of the jump, lets go of the sprint and makes a critical hit on the way down. Which of the two its next hit is, is decided tick by tick by what the agent is doing. What a player does to one that backs out of combos with S: backing off only makes room for the next jump.

    • punish

      public boolean punish
      Hit by the agent, it keeps its swing for its own way down and makes it a critical hit: the punish crit. Where it takes the full knockback the agent is out of its reach by then; where it takes part of it (as on a server that hands out less), the agent is right there with its sword on the way back.

    • timer

      public boolean timer
      It plays on the agent's rhythm, as a player does who has found out that the agent swings the moment its sword is all the way back and never before. It holds its distance a step outside the agent's reach and now and then steps into it and out again. Once the agent has swung, it takes a jump timed so that its critical hit comes down a tick or two before the agent's sword is back, when the agent has nothing to answer it with; an agent that comes in at it with its sword back it meets with a jump that has it on its way down as the agent arrives. Hit, it answers on its way down (punish). The friend of the user's who still beat it on 18 October did this.

    • spacer

      public boolean spacer
      The player at the edge of the reach, in two ways, as critChance has it swing by swing. For a critical hit: it keeps a step outside the agent's reach while its sword comes back, walks in and jumps from the edge of that reach once it is back, makes its critical hit on the way down, and backs straight out with S. Otherwise it stands where it is and hits the agent the moment it comes into reach. Never to the side, nothing late, nothing off. The user, 18 October: "crit and then PRESS S like go out of distance and Crit and go out of distance", and "PERFECT 3 block not moving", "just pure perfect combo"; the player is "mix of both".
